validator: draft 1 passed with no hard or soft problems; the faults below are the critic's
keep: The idea is named in two plain sentences up front: a still part's forces add to nothing, so drawing them and balancing them finds a force you cannot see.

The rule is stated in words (each leg's tension is half the weight divided by sin θ, θ from the horizontal) and worked with real numbers: 9.81 kN gives 5.66 kN a leg at 60° and 9.81 kN at 120°, tied to the Vectors ring so nothing is re-taught.

Thirteen screens: a still-have-it puzzle (1), then SHOW 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 alternating with DO 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, ending with two mixed puzzles (12, 13). Each brief misconception has its own wrong pick: force as something the load has (3), the leg gets weaker (9), friction as no force until it slides (11), half the load regardless of angle (5, 7), angle from the vertical read as from the horizontal (12), the hook carrying the sum of the legs (13).
Five footnotes, one per sentence, each on a rule or figure he would look up; no source named in the words.
fix: Causal step skipped: 'Anything that stays still has forces on it that add to nothing' gives no reason. Say any leftover force would start it moving.

Causal step skipped: 'the sideways parts pull against each other and cancel' gives no reason. Say the two legs lean the same amount in opposite directions, so their sideways parts are equal and opposite.

False absolute: 'Each force has a giver: something touching the part, or the Earth' leaves out other forces at a distance (a magnet). Say 'something touching it, or something pulling from a distance, like the Earth'.

The interactive brief names only the effect (the arrow grows). Name the cause too: each leg's vertical part stays at half the load while its sideways part grows. Draw each leg's vertical and sideways parts dashed.

The misconception is stated, not shown failing. Add one line with numbers: a leg that can safely take an example 8 kN is fine at 60° (5.66 kN) and overloaded at 120° (9.81 kN), with no change in the leg.
Practice arithmetic: '2.45 × 1.414 = 3.47' does not come out (it is 3.46). Work from 2452.5 N: 2452.5 × 1.414 = 3468 N, about 3.47 kN.
Practice's first line, 'well clear of 30° from the horizontal', is ambiguous. Say 'well above 30° from the horizontal'.
Analogy: 'each end holds up half the weight' is true only with level ends. Say so.
No recall checks (the lesson is taught, not tested) and no unreadable labels found: the three readouts are 18-25 characters and free to wrap.
